action.objective: Advance c5-c6 to cramp Black's position, preserving the c-pawn and creating a passed pawn threat, while keeping the rook and king safe.
action.rationale: Only c5c6 and g4g5 are commit_ready. c5c6 scored -1065 at depth 2 (exact) versus g4g5 -1242 at depth 3; both verified with no mate-in-one and tactical_refutation not_found. c5c6 keeps the pawn advanced on c6, restricts Black's knight and rook, and avoids g4g5's immediate Qxg5 capture threat to the g-pawn. Comparison is depth-limited, so I retain the uncertainty but prefer c5c6's healthier structure and lower material concession.
